title: Right extension of an encoded block
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over a finite alphabet $\Gamma$, let $q$ be one of its states, and let $s$ assign to each of its $k$ work tapes a possibly blank symbol and a Boolean. For any simulator input word, valid input-head position, output word, integer frontier $z$, and finite zipper stacks $l,r$, running the simulator for exactly $k$ steps from the forward-facing configuration in the right-extension phase with counter $0$ yields the configuration in that phase with counter $k$, still carrying $q$ and $s$, with frontier $z+k$, left stack equal to the reversed encoded guard block determined by $s$ prepended to $l$, and right stack obtained by dropping the first $k$ entries of $r$. The input-head position and output word are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Finite machine $M$ with finite state set and decidable equality
Read table $s$ assigning each tape a possibly blank symbol and a Boolean
replaced:
